subject: math
title: Telling Time and Elapsed Time
seo_title: Grade 3 Telling Time Worksheets: Nearest Minute and Elapsed Time (with Clocks)
standard_text: Tell and write time to the nearest minute, measure time intervals in minutes, and solve word problems about elapsed time.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 telling time worksheets with clock pictures: read the clock to the nearest 5 minutes and the nearest minute, quarter past and quarter to, a.m. and p.m., and elapsed time word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Short hand = hour. Long hand = minutes: count by 5s, then by 1s.
key_sub: If the short hand is between two numbers, use the smaller one. To find how much time passes, jump to the next hour first, then add the jumps.
body_html:
The two hands

  1. Hour: look at the short hand. If it is between two numbers, use the smaller one (between 3 and 4 means 3).
  2. Minutes: look at the long hand. Count by 5s for each number: 1 is 5, 2 is 10, 3 is 15 … 12 is 0.
  3. Write it: hour, colon, two-digit minutes: 3:25, 7:05, 10:00.
Long hand on123456789101112
Minutes5101520253035404550550

To the nearest minute

Between two numbers there are 5 small marks, one for each minute. Count by 5s to the last number the long hand passed, then count on by 1s.

Time words, a.m. and p.m.

WordsTimeMeans
o'clock4:00exactly on the hour
quarter past 44:1515 minutes after 4
half past 44:3030 minutes after 4
quarter to 54:4515 minutes before 5

a.m. is from midnight to noon: night and morning. p.m. is from noon to midnight: afternoon and evening. 1 hour = 60 minutes, half an hour = 30 minutes, a quarter hour = 15 minutes.

How much time passes (elapsed time)

Do not just subtract the minutes. Use a time line: jump to the next hour first, then jump to the end time, and add the jumps.

Find the end time

Ana starts reading at 4:35 p.m. and reads for 40 minutes. When does she finish?

4:35 + 25 minutes = 5:00. 40 − 25 = 15 more minutes: 5:15.

Answer: 5:15 p.m.

Find the start time

A show ended at 7:10 p.m. It lasted 30 minutes. When did it start?

Count back 10 minutes to 7:00, then 20 more minutes to 6:40.

Answer: 6:40 p.m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up the hands (reading 3:25 as 5:15)Short hand = hour, long hand = minutes
Reading 3:50 as 4:50 because the short hand is near the 4If the short hand has not reached the number, use the number before it
Reading the long hand on 5 as 5 minutesEach number on the clock is worth 5 minutes: 5 × 5 = 25
3:40 to 4:15 = 25 minutes (15 − 40)Jump to 4:00 first: 20 + 15 = 35 minutes

faq.q: When do kids learn to tell time to the nearest minute?
faq.a: In the Common Core, students tell time to the nearest hour and half hour in Grade 1, to the nearest five minutes in Grade 2, and to the nearest minute in Grade 3, along with elapsed time.

faq.q: How do you teach a child to read an analog clock?
faq.a: Read the short hand first for the hour, then count the long hand by 5s for the minutes. When the long hand is between numbers, count on by 1s from the last number it passed.
Elapsed time is how much time passes from a start time to an end time, such as from 3:40 to 4:15 (35 minutes).

faq.q: What is the easiest way to find elapsed time?
faq.a: Use a time line. Jump from the start time to the next hour, then from that hour to the end time, and add the jumps together.

faq.q: What do a.m. and p.m. mean?
faq.a: a.m. is used for times from midnight to noon, and p.m. is used for times from noon to midnight.

items.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
items.e: The long hand goes all the way around the clock once in one hour: 60 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter hour?
items.e: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes.

items.q: School starts in the morning. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 8:00 a.m.
a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 3:15 p.m.

items.q: You eat dinner in the evening. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 6:30 p.m.

items.q: Which time is after midnight and before noon?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 7:20 a.m.

items.q: You go to bed at night. Which time could it be?
items.e: a.m. is from midnight to noon (night and morning). p.m. is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). The answer is 9:00 p.m.
11:45 is 15 minutes before 12:00, so it is quarter to 12.
7:30 is 30 minutes after 7:00, so it is half past 7.
4:15 is 15 minutes after 4:00, so it is quarter past 4.

items.q: How much time passes from 8:30 to 9:00?
items.e: From 8:30 to the next hour, 9:00, is 60 − 30 = 30 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 6:00 to 6:25?
items.e: Count on from 6:00 to 6:25: 25 − 0 = 25 minutes.

items.q: How much time passes from 10:30 to 10:40?

items.q: How much time passes from 4:10 to 4:40?

items.q: How much time passes from 2:20 to 2:35?

items.q: How much time passes from 2:20 to 2:40?

items.q: Maya got to the park at 4:35 p.m. and left at 5:25 p.m. How long was Maya there?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 4:35 to 5:00 is 25 minutes. Then 5:00 to 5:25 is 25 minutes. 25 + 25 = 50 minutes.

items.q: Sam got to the library at 3:45 p.m. and left at 4:30 p.m. How long was Sam there?
items.e: Jump to the next hour first: 3:45 to 4:00 is 15 minutes. Then 4:00 to 4:30 is 30 minutes. 15 + 30 = 45 minutes.
